claims.claim: the measured w98c row respawns without `--force`: a keyed-but-idle roster entry (Q1 says live), no outcome record, past the dispatch grace window, transcript tail `API Error: stream closed before completion` now reaches the dispatch boundary, and the old session is STILL stopped (`claude stop <job-ref>`) and tombstoned (`stopped`), with the acceptance announced on stderr. Before this lane the identical drive raised `w: turn is running -- pass --force to interrupt it first, or wait for it to finish`.

the acceptance reads the PROBE's verdict, not the persisted `status` string: the fixture record still says `working` (it was never rewritten, exactly as w98c's was) and is accepted because `recompute_worker_native` concludes `dead-suspected` for it. A guard that read `record["status"]` would refuse.

the marker set is the MEASURED stream-death family, not one string: all four texts tallied from real `isApiErrorMessage` records on this host (`stream closed before completion`, `Connection lost mid-response`, `Server error mid-response`, `The response stopped arriving`) are accepted.

the refusal survives for every row that is genuinely running a turn, and each of the four refusal tests also proves the acceptance exists, so a blanket refusal cannot satisfy them: a roster `busy` entry (the probe says `working`), a 429 `limited` tail, no transcript evidence at all, and a death buried under newer chatter each refuse with `turn is running` while the same row with the one differing fact changed reaches dispatch.
